items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 2課 · 範囲の始まり・限度

items.q: 日常のおかずから高級料理の食材（ ）、この店にないものはない。
items.qr: Nichijou no okazu kara koukyuu ryouri no shokuzai (___), kono mise ni nai mono wa nai.
items.en: From everyday side dishes right up to ingredients for fine cuisine, there's nothing this shop doesn't have.
items.why: 〜から〜に至るまで shows a wide range (everyday ↔ luxury), matching ないものはない. a) needs a time word and an ending. b) downplays an amount — the opposite of "everything".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 2課 · 範囲の始まり・限度

items.q: 3歳の息子がやってくれる手伝いは、洗濯物をかごに入れるとか新聞を運ぶ（ ）、あまり役に立ちません。
items.qr: Sansai no musuko ga yatte kureru tetsudai wa, sentakumono o kago ni ireru toka shinbun o hakobu (___), amari yaku ni tachimasen.
items.en: The help my three-year-old son gives amounts to no more than putting laundry in the basket or carrying the newspaper, so it isn't much use.
items.why: The examples are small chores, and the sentence ends あまり役に立ちません — so the speaker is downplaying the help → といったところで (connective form of 〜といったところだ). a) would stress how wide the range of help is, the opposite message. c) 限りで marks a time limit and attaches to time nouns, not to verbs like 運ぶ.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 2課 · 範囲の始まり・限度

items.q: これほど多種多様な機能を持ったものは、わが社の（ ）をおいてほかにないと自負しております。
items.qr: Kore hodo tashu tayou na kinou o motta mono wa, waga sha no (___) o oite hoka ni nai to jifu shite orimasu.
items.en: We take pride in the fact that nothing but this product of ours offers such a wide variety of functions.
items.why: をおいて attaches straight to the thing being rated highly. a) だけ clashes with をおいてほかにない, which already means "only" — it doubles up. b) 素晴らしさ is a quality, but the sentence compares things (もの) with many functions.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: この力仕事を任せられる人は、（ ）をおいてほかにいない。
items.qr: Kono chikara shigoto o makaserareru hito wa, (___) o oite hoka ni inai.
items.en: There's no one but Mr. Yamaguchi we can entrust this heavy work to.
items.why: The noun must be a specific one the speaker rates highly. a) fits. b) 男性 is a whole category — "no one except men" is not praise of a unique person. c) わたし: you don't use をおいて to praise yourself, since it expresses the speaker's high evaluation of something else.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: わたしがやっていけそうな仕事は、教師をおいて（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi ga yatte ikesou na shigoto wa, kyoushi o oite (___).
items.en: The only job I could probably make a go of is teaching — there's surely nothing else.

opts.t: ほかにもあるだろうか
opts.r: hoka ni mo aru darou ka

items.why: をおいて must close with a negative "there's no other" — あるまい = ないだろう. a) ほかにも…だろうか opens up the possibility of other jobs, contradicting "only teaching". c) わからない is negative in form but doesn't say "there's no other".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: この絵には、（ ）ならではの純真さがあると思う。
items.qr: Kono e ni wa, (___) nara de wa no junshinsa ga aru to omou.
items.en: I think this picture has an innocence that only a child could have.
items.why: ならでは + a fine quality unique to the noun: innocence belongs to children. b) innocence isn't what's special about adults. c) you don't praise yourself with ならでは — it expresses the speaker's admiration for something else.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: こんな（ ）字は、林さんならではだ。
items.qr: Konna (___) ji wa, Hayashi-san nara de wa da.
items.en: Only Ms. Hayashi could write such beautiful characters.
items.why: ならでは is always praise (素晴らしいことを実現できる). a) and b) are negative qualities, which ならでは can never introduce.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: 会の最後に木村さんが詩を読んだ。この道のプロならではの朗読に、わたしは（ ）。
items.qr: Kai no saigo ni Kimura-san ga shi o yonda. Kono michi no puro nara de wa no roudoku ni, watashi wa (___).
items.en: At the end of the event Mr. Kimura read a poem. I was deeply moved by a recitation only a true professional could give.

opts.t: あまり期待していなかった

items.why: プロならではの朗読 praises the reading, so the reaction must be positive → c). a) contradicts the praise; b) describes expectations before the reading, not the reaction to it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: 母のケーキ作りは単なる趣味にとどまらず、（ ）までになった。
items.qr: Haha no keeki-zukuri wa tan naru shumi ni todomarazu, (___) made ni natta.
items.en: My mother's cake-making went beyond a mere hobby — she even ended up opening her own shop.

opts.t: いろいろな店のケーキを食べる
opts.r: iroiro na mise no keeki o taberu

items.why: The second clause must go beyond the hobby into a wider sphere — running a business does. a) tasty cakes is still within a hobby. c) eating other shops' cakes isn't a wider version of making cakes at all.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: 鈴木氏の研究成果は（ ）にとどまらず、広く産業界でも注目されている。
items.qr: Suzuki-shi no kenkyuu seika wa (___) ni todomarazu, hiroku sangyoukai de mo chuumoku sarete iru.
items.en: Mr. Suzuki's research results are attracting attention not just within his academic society but widely in industry too.
items.why: The noun must be a limited range that the second clause (広く産業界でも) goes beyond. A specialist academic society → the wider world of industry. b) 日本国内 is geographic, while 産業界 is a field, so it isn't a wider version of it. c) 世界中 is already a very wide range — "not limited to the whole world" makes no sense.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: 今、この服は（ ）大人気だそうだ。
items.qr: Ima, kono fuku wa (___) daininki da sou da.
items.en: I hear these clothes are now hugely popular not only with a small group of women but with lots of people.

opts.t: 女性にとどまらず男性には
opts.r: josei ni todomarazu dansei ni wa
opts.en: not limited to women, among men

opts.t: わたしにとどまらず母にも
opts.r: watashi ni todomarazu haha ni mo
opts.en: not limited to me, my mother too

opts.t: 一部の女性にとどまらず多くの人に
opts.r: ichibu no josei ni todomarazu ooku no hito ni
opts.en: not limited to some women, with many people

items.why: The wider range must include the first one: 多くの人 includes 一部の女性. a) 男性 is a separate group, not a larger one (and は doesn't give the "also" sense needed). b) 母 is just another person; わたし → 母 isn't a broadening, and わたし isn't a "limited range or phenomenon".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: うちの父は（ ）母に任せている。
items.qr: Uchi no chichi wa (___) haha ni makasete iru.
items.en: My father leaves everything to my mother — not just the housework but even what he himself wears.

opts.t: 家事はおろか自分の着る物のことさえ
opts.r: kaji wa oroka jibun no kiru mono no koto sae
opts.en: not just housework but even his own clothes

opts.t: 身の回りのことはおろか家の掃除さえ
opts.r: mi no mawari no koto wa oroka ie no souji sae
opts.en: not just his personal things but even cleaning the house

opts.t: 自分の仕事はおろか子供の教育さえ
opts.r: jibun no shigoto wa oroka kodomo no kyouiku sae
opts.en: not just his own work but even the children's education

items.why: X はおろか Y さえ: X is the obvious case, Y the more extreme one. Leaving housework to his wife is (sadly) common; leaving even his own clothes to her is extreme. b) is reversed — his personal belongings are the more personal, extreme item, house cleaning the ordinary one. c) mixes unrelated scales; handing over his own job to his wife isn't the "obvious" starting point.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: 当時はお金がなかったので、（ ）はおろか学費もぎりぎりだった。
items.qr: Touji wa okane ga nakatta node, (___) wa oroka gakuhi mo girigiri datta.
items.en: I had no money back then, so never mind spending money — even my tuition was barely covered.
items.why: The obvious lack (money for fun) comes before はおろか, the more serious one (tuition) after it with も. b) 食費 is at least as essential as tuition, so the scale doesn't climb. c) アルバイト代 is income, not something you lack money for.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: わたしは外国旅行はおろか（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi wa gaikoku ryokou wa oroka (___).
items.en: Forget travelling abroad — I've never even been outside the prefecture I live in.

opts.t: 国内では何度も旅行した
opts.r: kokunai de wa nando mo ryokou shita
opts.en: I've travelled many times in Japan

opts.t: 住んでいる県から出たこともない
opts.r: sunde iru ken kara deta koto mo nai
opts.en: I've never even left my prefecture

opts.t: 県外にはあまり行かない
opts.en: I don't often go outside the prefecture

items.why: The second part must be the extreme, negative case with も/さえ: never even left the prefecture. a) is positive and contrasts rather than intensifies. c) あまり行かない is a weak, partial statement with no も — not "even more so".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: その国では、（ ）もさることながら、伝統的な工芸品の買い物が楽しめる。
items.qr: Sono kuni de wa, (___) mo saru koto nagara, dentouteki na kougeihin no kaimono ga tanoshimeru.
items.en: In that country, sightseeing is great of course, but you can enjoy shopping for traditional crafts even more.
items.why: もさることながら accepts the first item and adds something on the same side that's even more worth stressing. Both must be attractions: 観光 and crafts shopping. a) and c) are negatives — they can't be "~ is true, and even better…" for something enjoyable.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: 試合に勝つには選手の実力もさることながら、（ ）。
items.qr: Shiai ni katsu ni wa senshu no jitsuryoku mo saru koto nagara, (___).
items.en: To win a match, the players' ability matters, of course, but luck is needed too.

opts.r: un mo hitsuyou na no da
un wa kankei nai no da
opts.en: luck has nothing to do with it

items.why: The second clause adds a further point to stress about what's needed to win → 運も必要. b) denies a point rather than adding one. c) is an explanation of one past result, which doesn't match the general 〜には ("in order to win").
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: 彼の趣味は広い。料理を（ ）、料理に合う食器を作ることも趣味だと言う。
items.qr: Kare no shumi wa hiroi. Ryouri o (___), ryouri ni au shokki o tsukuru koto mo shumi da to iu.
items.en: He has wide-ranging hobbies. He says he doesn't just cook — making tableware to go with his dishes is a hobby too.
items.why: にとどまらず takes the dictionary form of a verb directly and extends to a wider activity (cooking → making tableware). b) 〜に限らず normally attaches to nouns (料理に限らず), so 作るに限らず is unnatural. c) 〜とは限らない means "not necessarily" — a completely different meaning.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: この景色は富士山の頂上（ ）のものだろう。よく見ておこう。
items.qr: Kono keshiki wa Fujisan no choujou (___) no mono darou. Yoku mite okou.
items.en: This view must be one you can only get from the summit of Mt. Fuji. Let's take a good look.
items.why: 〜ならではの N: a fine thing only possible at that place → 頂上ならではの(もの). a) 限りのもの doesn't mean "unique to". c) をおいて must be followed by ほかにない／いない, not by の + noun.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: この病気を治す方法は、今のところ手術（ ）ほかにないのです。
items.qr: Kono byouki o naosu houhou wa, ima no tokoro shujutsu (___) hoka ni nai no desu.
items.en: For now, there's no way to cure this disease other than surgery.
items.why: The sentence ends ほかにない → 〜をおいてほかにない. b) ならでは is followed by の + N or だ, and praises something special. c) はおろか needs a second, more extreme item with も/さえ — there isn't one.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: わたしはスペイン語では会話（ ）簡単なあいさつもできない。
items.qr: Watashi wa Supeingo de wa kaiwa (___) kantan na aisatsu mo dekinai.
items.en: In Spanish I can't even manage a simple greeting, let alone a conversation.
items.why: Obvious case (conversation) → extreme case with も (even a simple greeting), negative overall → はおろか. a) をおいて needs ほかにない. c) にとどまらず expands to a wider positive range; here the second item is a smaller, more basic skill that is also missing.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: 年金の問題（ ）、少子化対策は政府の大きな課題である。
items.qr: Nenkin no mondai (___), shoushika taisaku wa seifu no ookina kadai de aru.
items.en: The pension problem is one thing, but measures against the falling birth rate are an even bigger challenge for the government.
items.why: Both items are serious issues; the first is acknowledged and the second stressed more → もさることながら. a) はおろか needs も／さえ on the second item and a climb in degree inside a mostly negative "can't even" sentence. b) をおいて needs ほかにない at the end.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 3課 · 限定・非限定・付加

items.q: あの部屋はかなり寒いから、長い時間いるなら上着なり（ ）なりが必要だろう。
items.qr: Ano heya wa kanari samui kara, nagai jikan iru nara uwagi nari (___) nari ga hitsuyou darou.
items.en: That room is pretty cold, so if you'll be there a long time you'll probably need a jacket or a lap blanket or something.
items.why: なり…なり lists examples from the same group in the same form: 上着 (a thing you wear) ↔ ひざ掛け (a thing you put over yourself). a) is a verb phrase next to a noun and a different kind of measure; c) 防寒 is the purpose itself, not an item like 上着.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 着ない服は人にあげるなりフリーマーケットに出すなりして、（ ）。
items.qr: Kinai fuku wa hito ni ageru nari furii maaketto ni dasu nari shite, (___).
items.en: Let's sort out the clothes we don't wear — give them away, put them in a flea market, whatever.
items.why: The book: after なり…なり no past-tense sentence — it ends with a wish, intention or appeal. c) 〜よう is an intention/invitation. a) is past; b) is a past experience.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 1年に2、3度、ハイキングなりキャンプなり遊びに（ ）。
items.qr: Ichinen ni ni, sando, haikingu nari kyanpu nari asobi ni (___).
items.en: How about going out two or three times a year — hiking, camping, whatever?
items.why: An invitation (働きかけ) is exactly what なり…なり sets up. b) is past. c) reports a fixed past decision — no suggestion, and also past tense.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 電話なりメールなり（ ）。
items.qr: Denwa nari meeru nari (___).
items.en: There must be some way to let them know — by phone, by email, whatever.

opts.t: どちらで知らせますか
opts.en: which will you use to tell them?

opts.t: 知らせる方法はあるはずですよ
opts.r: shiraseru houhou wa aru hazu desu yo
opts.en: there must be a way to let them know

opts.t: 知らせる方法が何もない
opts.r: shiraseru houhou ga nani mo nai
opts.en: there's no way at all to let them know

items.why: なり…なり avoids choosing ("anything will do") to nudge the listener — b) is that nudge ("you can surely tell them somehow"). a) asks for a specific choice, which defeats the point of "any of them". c) is a flat negative statement, not advice.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 社長であろうと（ ）であろうと、自分の会社を大切に思っているはずだ。
items.qr: Shachou de arou to (___) de arou to, jibun no kaisha o taisetsu ni omotte iru hazu da.
items.en: Whether president or rank-and-file employee, everyone should care about their own company.
items.why: であろうと…であろうと pairs two members of the same group — here, positions in a company hierarchy: the top (社長) and the bottom (平社員), meaning "everyone, whatever their rank". a) 正社員 is an employment type, not a rank on the same scale; c) サラリーマン is a broad category of worker, not a position opposite 社長.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 検査の結果、ある病気が見つかった。これから先、通院であれ入院であれ（ ）。
items.qr: Kensa no kekka, aru byouki ga mitsukatta. Kore kara saki, tsuuin de are nyuuin de are (___).
items.en: The tests found an illness. From now on, whether it's outpatient visits or a hospital stay, I'll have more to worry about.

opts.en: it has been decided I'll do (it)

opts.t: 選ばなければならない

items.why: であれ…であれ = "no matter which, the same holds". a) is true either way. b) reports a decision about something specific — it doesn't hold "regardless". c) choosing between them contradicts "it doesn't matter which".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 与党であれ野党であれ、（ ）。
items.qr: Yotou de are yatou de are, (___).
items.en: Ruling party or opposition, I want them all to fight the election campaign properly.

opts.t: わたしは選挙の結果に関心がある
opts.r: watashi wa senkyo no kekka ni kanshin ga aru
opts.en: I'm interested in the election results

opts.t: 選挙でどちらが勝つだろうか
opts.r: senkyo de dochira ga katsu darou ka
opts.en: I wonder which will win the election

opts.t: 選挙戦をしっかり頑張ってほしい
opts.en: I want them to fight the campaign properly

items.why: The main clause must apply equally to both parties — c) does (and unlike といい／といわず, であれ can end with a wish). a) is about the speaker, not about the parties. b) asks which one, which contradicts "whichever it is".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: （ ）、このパソコンは最高だ。
items.qr: (___), kono pasokon wa saikou da.
items.en: Both in its features and its size, this computer is the best.

opts.t: 機能といい大きさといい
opts.r: kinou to ii ookisa to ii
opts.en: both its features and its size

opts.t: 簡単だといい値段といい
opts.r: kantan da to ii nedan to ii

opts.t: 便利だといい安いといい
opts.r: benri da to ii yasui to ii

items.why: といい attaches to nouns (🔗 名＋といい), and both items should be the same kind of thing — two aspects of the PC. b) and c) put といい after adjective/だ forms (簡単だ, 便利だ, 安い), which this pattern doesn't allow; b) also mixes an adjective with a noun.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 庭といい玄関といい、（ ）。
items.qr: Niwa to ii genkan to ii, (___).
items.en: The garden, the entrance — they're both covered in rubbish.

opts.t: きれいに掃いてください
掃除しなければきれいにならない
opts.en: they won't get clean unless cleaned

items.why: After といい comes a state (the speaker's assessment) — b). a) is a request (働きかけ), which the book bans. c) is a general conditional truth, not a description of how the garden and entrance look now.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: この地方は山といい川といい、（ ）。いつか行ってみたい。
items.qr: Kono chihou wa yama to ii kawa to ii, (___). Itsuka itte mitai.
items.en: In this region the mountains and rivers alike are beautiful this time of year. I'd like to go someday.

opts.t: 今の季節はとてもきれいだ
opts.r: ima no kisetsu wa totemo kirei da

items.why: といい leads to the speaker's evaluation (形容詞文) — b) きれいだ. a) just states quantity/existence, not an assessment. c) is a one-off past event, not a state.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 水泳といいテニスといい、（ ）。
items.qr: Suiei to ii tenisu to ii, (___).
items.en: Swimming, tennis — sports are all fun.

opts.t: スポーツはみな楽しい
わたしは子供に習わせている
opts.r: watashi wa kodomo ni narawasete iru
opts.en: I'm having my child take lessons

opts.t: わたしはやったことがない
opts.r: watashi wa yatta koto ga nai

items.why: An evaluative adjective sentence (楽しい) is the natural follow-up. b) is an action the speaker is taking; c) is the speaker's experience (and negative) — neither judges swimming and tennis.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: うちの娘は壁といわず（ ）といわず、あちこちに好きなアイドルの写真をはっている。
items.qr: Uchi no musume wa kabe to iwazu (___) to iwazu, achikochi ni suki na aidoru no shashin o hatte iru.
items.en: My daughter has stuck photos of her favourite idol everywhere — on the walls, on the ceiling, all over.
items.why: といわず…といわず usually pairs words that are connected in space or time: 壁 and 天井 are neighbouring surfaces of a room, together meaning "all over the room". a) bag and c) notebook are objects, not part of the same space as 壁.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: あの通りは昼といわず夜といわず（ ）。
items.qr: Ano toori wa hiru to iwazu yoru to iwazu (___).
items.en: That street is bustling day and night alike.
items.why: The book's ban list for といわず: no negative sentences, no appeals to the listener. a) is negative; b) is a request. c) is a state that holds "all the time".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: 虫といわず魚といわず、（ ）。
items.qr: Mushi to iwazu sakana to iwazu, (___).
items.en: Bugs, fish — my child wants to catch anything and everything.

opts.t: うちの子は何でも捕まえたがる
opts.r: uchi no ko wa nan demo tsukamaetagaru
opts.en: my child wants to catch anything

opts.t: 何でも早く捨てなさい
opts.en: throw it all away at once!
I don't want to keep any

items.why: といわず can be followed by a verb sentence describing behaviour (book ③), and it's often slightly negative in image (a child grabbing every creature). b) is a command and c) a negative — both banned.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: （ ）、この店の料理は素晴らしい。
items.qr: (___), kono mise no ryouri wa subarashii.
items.en: In both taste and presentation, this restaurant's food is superb.

opts.t: 味といい盛り付けといい
opts.r: aji to ii moritsuke to ii

opts.t: 味といわず盛り付けといわず
opts.r: aji to iwazu moritsuke to iwazu

items.why: Judging the food from two angles and giving a verdict (素晴らしい) → といい. a) なり…なり needs a suggestion or request at the end. c) といわず is for things connected in time/space meaning "everywhere / always", usually negative — not for praising aspects of a dish.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: （ ）、何か筆記用具をここに置いておいたほうがいいです。
items.qr: (___), nanika hikki yougu o koko ni oite oita hou ga ii desu.
items.en: You should leave something to write with here — a pencil, a ballpoint, anything.

opts.t: 鉛筆なりボールペンなり
opts.en: a pencil or a ballpoint, whichever

opts.t: 鉛筆といいボールペンといい
opts.r: enpitsu to ii boorupen to ii

opts.t: 鉛筆といわずボールペンといわず
opts.r: enpitsu to iwazu boorupen to iwazu

items.why: 何か (something — anything will do) + advice 〜たほうがいい → なり…なり. b) といい can't be followed by advice/appeals. c) といわず can't be followed by an appeal either, and it means "all of them, everywhere", not "one of them".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: （ ）、人との接し方が大切なのだ。
items.qr: (___), hito to no sesshikata ga taisetsu na no da.
items.en: Whether you're a restaurant worker or an office worker, how you deal with people is what matters.

opts.t: レストランの店員なり会社員なり
opts.r: resutoran no ten'in nari kaishain nari
opts.en: restaurant staff or office worker, whichever

opts.t: レストランの店員であれ会社員であれ
opts.r: resutoran no ten'in de are kaishain de are
opts.en: whether restaurant staff or office worker

opts.t: レストランの店員といわず会社員といわず
opts.r: resutoran no ten'in to iwazu kaishain to iwazu
opts.en: restaurant staff and office workers alike

items.why: A general truth that holds for every member of a group (kinds of working people) → であれ…であれ. a) なり…なり would need a suggestion ("become one or the other"), not a general statement. c) といわず pairs space/time neighbours and describes a widespread (often negative) state, not a principle.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: この名所には（ ）、一年中観光客が訪れる。
items.qr: Kono meisho ni wa (___), ichinenjuu kankoukyaku ga otozureru.
items.en: Tourists visit this famous spot all year round — spring, autumn, any season.

opts.r: haru to ii aki to ii

opts.t: 春といわず秋といわず
opts.r: haru to iwazu aki to iwazu
opts.en: spring and autumn alike — all the time

items.why: Time-connected pair + 一年中 ("all the time") + a plain verb sentence (訪れる) → といわず. a) needs a suggestion. b) といい needs an evaluation (〜は美しい), not an event like visitors coming.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: （ ）、フォークで食べるのは変だ。
items.qr: (___), fooku de taberu no wa hen da.
items.en: Be it sushi or sashimi, eating it with a fork is weird.

opts.t: すしであれさしみであれ
opts.r: sushi de are sashimi de are

opts.t: すしといわずさしみといわず
opts.r: sushi to iwazu sashimi to iwazu

items.why: "Whichever of these Japanese dishes it is, the same judgement applies" → であれ…であれ. a) なり…なり must end in advice/a request, and 変だ is a judgement. c) といわず is for space/time neighbours meaning "everywhere/always"; sushi and sashimi aren't that kind of pair.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 4課 · 例示

items.q: （ ）いかんで入院するかしないかを決めるのだそうです。
items.qr: (___) ikan de nyuuin suru ka shinai ka o kimeru no da sou desu.
items.en: Apparently they'll decide whether or not to hospitalise him depending on the results of today's tests.

opts.en: whether there is a free bed

items.why: いかん attaches to words with a range of variation (違いや幅がある意味の言葉). Test results can be anything from fine to serious. a) consent and b) 有無 (yes/no) are simple either/or matters — for those you'd say 〜によって or 〜があるかどうかで.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 父は、体調いかんでは、（ ）。
items.qr: Chichi wa, taichou ikan de wa, (___).
items.en: Depending on his health, my father might quit his company.

opts.t: 役職を続けるかどうか迷っているらしい
opts.r: yakushoku o tsuzukeru ka dou ka mayotte iru rashii
opts.en: he seems to be unsure whether to stay in his post

opts.t: その日の仕事の量を変えているようだ
opts.r: sono hi no shigoto no ryou o kaete iru you da
opts.en: he seems to change his workload each day

opts.t: 会社を辞めるかもしれない
opts.r: kaisha o yameru ka mo shirenai

items.why: After 〜いかんでは comes one possible outcome among several (いろいろな事態のうち可能性があるもの) — 〜かもしれない is exactly that. a) is a present state of mind, not a possible outcome. b) is a habitual adjustment, which takes 体調によって／体調いかんで, not the "one possibility" form では.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 宣伝方法いかんで（ ）。
items.qr: Senden houhou ikan de (___).
items.en: Sales are swayed by the advertising method.

opts.t: 売り上げが左右される

items.why: What follows いかんで must say the outcome changes or gets decided (変わる・決まる). 左右される ("is swayed") is exactly that. a) and c) are single completed results — they don't express dependence at all.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 党首のやる気いかんで（ ）。
items.qr: Toushu no yaruki ikan de (___).
items.en: The election result will be decided by how motivated the party leader is.
items.why: Same rule — 〜いかんで + 決まる. b) is a past fact with no open outcome. c) is a wish, which doesn't express "depends on".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: （ ）のいかんによらず、一度購入されたチケットの払い戻しはいたしません。
items.qr: (___) no ikan ni yorazu, ichido kounyuu sareta chiketto no haraimodoshi wa itashimasen.
items.en: Whatever the reason, we do not refund tickets once they have been purchased.
items.why: The noun must cover the whole range (any reason, good or bad). 理由 does. b) and c) have already fixed one value on the dial — "regardless of what kind of unjustified reason" makes no sense.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: （ ）のいかんを問わず、優秀な社員を募集している。
items.qr: (___) no ikan o towazu, yuushuu na shain o boshuu shite iru.
items.en: We are recruiting talented staff, regardless of educational background.
items.why: 学歴 ranges widely (high school, university, graduate school…). a) 男女 and c) 国内か国外か are two-way choices — Japanese uses plain 〜を問わず for those (男女を問わず, 国内外を問わず), not いかん.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: スピーチ大会では、内容のいかんにかかわらず、（ ）。
items.qr: Supiichi taikai de wa, naiyou no ikan ni kakawarazu, (___).
items.en: At the speech contest, everyone is given a participation prize regardless of what their speech is about.

opts.t: みんな時間オーバーだった
全員に参加賞が与えられる
opts.en: everyone is given a participation prize

items.why: What follows must show something not affected by the content — a fixed rule (c). a) and b) are just observations of what happened; they don't contrast with "the content could vary".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 借りたお金は金額いかんにかかわらず、（ ）。
items.qr: Karita okane wa kingaku ikan ni kakawarazu, (___).
items.en: Borrowed money should be paid back quickly, whatever the amount.

opts.en: I should have returned it last week

items.why: A general obligation that holds for any amount → a). b) comments on the amount itself — the very thing that's supposed to be irrelevant. c) is a memory of a past event, unrelated to "regardless of the amount".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 中川選手は（ ）をものともせずに、終始冷静にプレーした。
items.qr: Nakagawa senshu wa (___) o mono to mo sezu ni, shuushi reisei ni puree shita.
items.en: Undaunted by the pressure, Nakagawa played calmly from start to finish.
items.why: The noun must be a real obstacle (大きな障害になるような状況). Pressure is one. b) teammates and c) cheering are help, not obstacles — there's nothing to overcome.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: この会社は（ ）をものともせずに、順調に売り上げを伸ばしている。
items.qr: Kono kaisha wa (___) o mono to mo sezu ni, junchou ni uriage o nobashite iru.
items.en: Undeterred by the recession, this company is steadily increasing its sales.
items.why: 不況 (recession) is a situation that would normally drag sales down — an obstacle to beat. a) products and c) work are neutral, not hardships.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 今年90歳になる高橋さんは、足腰の痛みをものともせず、（ ）。
items.qr: Kotoshi kyuujussai ni naru Takahashi-san wa, ashikoshi no itami o mono to mo sezu, (___).
items.en: Mr. Takahashi, who turns 90 this year, is devoting himself to coaching young people, undaunted by the pain in his legs and back.

opts.t: 病院に行こうとしない

opts.en: is putting up with a lot

opts.t: 若い人の指導に励んでいる
opts.r: wakai hito no shidou ni hagende iru
opts.en: is devoted to coaching young people

items.why: The sentence must praise courage: overcoming the obstacle and acting positively (c). a) stubbornly avoiding hospital isn't admirable, and b) just enduring the pain isn't "acting in spite of it" — neither is the brave action the pattern requires.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 兄は事業の失敗をものともせず、（ ）。
items.qr: Ani wa jigyou no shippai o mono to mo sezu, (___).
items.en: Undaunted by the failure of his business, my older brother is tackling a new job.

opts.t: 相変わらず借金を繰り返した
opts.en: kept on borrowing money as usual

opts.t: 会社を辞めてしまった
新しい仕事に取り組んでいる

items.why: Only c) is a positive, courageous follow-up worth praising. a) repeating debts is criticism, not praise. b) quitting means he gave in to the setback — the opposite of をものともせず.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 彼は（ ）をよそに、危険な仕事を続けた。
items.qr: Kare wa (___) o yoso ni, kiken na shigoto o tsuzuketa.
items.en: Ignoring the objections of those around him, he carried on with his dangerous work.

opts.en: the objections of those around him

items.why: をよそに attaches to the surrounding situation — typically other people's reactions (周りの状況を表す言葉). a) fits. b) an injury is a personal obstacle → 足のけがをものともせず. c) 体力 is neither a surrounding situation nor something to ignore.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: （ ）をよそに、彼はまた早朝からサーフィンに出かけて行った。
items.qr: (___) o yoso ni, kare wa mata souchou kara saafin ni dekakete itta.
items.en: Paying no heed to his parents' worries, he went off surfing again early in the morning.
items.why: Other people's feelings that he treats as "none of his business" → 親の心配をよそに, with the exasperated tone of また (again!). a) lack of funds and c) tiredness are his own obstacles (→ をものともせず), not the surroundings he's ignoring.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 国民の期待をよそに、（ ）。
items.qr: Kokumin no kitai o yoso ni, (___).
items.en: In disregard of the public's expectations, the new government continued with the old policies.

opts.t: 新政府は新しいことをやろうとしている
opts.r: shinseifu wa atarashii koto o yarou to shite iru
opts.en: the new government is trying to do new things

opts.t: 新政府の政策は新しくない
opts.r: shinseifu no seisaku wa atarashiku nai
opts.en: the new government's policies aren't new

opts.t: 新政府は従来の政策を続けた
opts.r: shinseifu wa juurai no seisaku o tsuzuketa
opts.en: the new government continued the old policies

items.why: What follows must be an action that ignores the situation (状況を無視したような行動). c) is that action. a) meets the expectations rather than ignoring them. b) is a description of a state, not an action by a subject.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: （ ）ならいざしらず、普通の人は自分の経験をそんなに簡単に文章化できない。
items.qr: (___) nara iza shirazu, futsuu no hito wa jibun no keiken o sonna ni kantan ni bunshouka dekinai.
items.en: A novelist might, but ordinary people can't put their experiences into writing that easily.
items.why: A ならいざしらず B — A and B must be the same kind of thing at opposite ends. B is 普通の人 (a person), so A must be a person: 小説家. b) a novel is a thing, not a person. a) is an action and would also need の (小説を書くのならいざしらず); it still wouldn't parallel 普通の人.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 5歳の子供ならいざしらず、（ ）がこんなことを知らないなんておかしい。
items.qr: Gosai no kodomo nara iza shirazu, (___) ga konna koto o shiranai nante okashii.
items.en: For a five-year-old it would be one thing, but it's strange for an adult not to know something like this.
items.why: The second half must be the opposite extreme (対極にある例) of a 5-year-old — an adult. b) a 6-year-old is almost the same, so there's no contrast. c) a 3-year-old is even younger — being ignorant would be more natural, not "strange".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: （ ）ならいざしらず、普通の人間が国民を自由に動かせるはずはない。
items.qr: (___) nara iza shirazu, futsuu no ningen ga kokumin o jiyuu ni ugokaseru hazu wa nai.
items.en: A president might be able to, but there's no way an ordinary person can move the whole nation as they please.
items.why: The extreme example opposite to 普通の人間 is someone with enormous power — a president. a) "I" is not an extreme case (and is effectively an ordinary person). c) 一市民 is an ordinary person — same side as B, no contrast.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 世界一周旅行をするのならいざしらず、日帰り旅行には（ ）。
items.qr: Sekai isshuu ryokou o suru no nara iza shirazu, higaeri ryokou ni wa (___).
items.en: If you were going round the world, maybe — but you don't need a bag that big for a day trip.

opts.t: そんな大きなかばんは要らない
opts.en: you don't need such a big bag

opts.t: 一人1万円ぐらいかかる
opts.en: it costs about 10,000 yen per person

opts.t: わたしは行きたくない

items.why: What follows should express exasperation about the ordinary case, contrasting with the extreme one: "a round-the-world trip would justify a big bag, a day trip doesn't" (a). b) is a neutral fact with no link to the contrast. c) is a personal wish, not a reaction to someone overdoing it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 本人の頑張り（ ）素晴らしい結果が出るかもしれない。
items.qr: Honnin no ganbari (___) subarashii kekka ga deru ka mo shirenai.
items.en: Depending on how hard he works, he may get a wonderful result.
items.why: 〜かもしれない names one possible outcome that depends on his effort → いかんでは. b) would say effort makes no difference — contradicting the sentence. c) needs an extreme example and a contrasting complaint.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 田中さんは周囲の反対（ ）、その実験を続けている。
items.qr: Tanaka-san wa shuui no hantai (___), sono jikken o tsuzukete iru.
items.en: Undaunted by the opposition around him, Mr. Tanaka is carrying on with that experiment.

opts.r: o mono to mo sezu ni

items.why: Opposition is an obstacle he pushes past, and carrying on with research reads as admirable → をものともせずに. (をよそに would also fit 周囲の反対, but it isn't offered.) a) 反対 is not a noun with a range of values ("regardless of how much opposition" is not what's meant), and the follow-up isn't a fixed rule. c) there's no extreme-vs-ordinary contrast.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: 明さんは周囲の非難（ ）、就職しないで家でぶらぶらしている。
items.qr: Akira-san wa shuui no hinan (___), shuushoku shinaide ie de burabura shite iru.
items.en: Paying no heed to the criticism around him, Akira lazes around at home without getting a job.

opts.r: o mono to mo sezu ni

items.why: Lazing about at home is nothing to admire — the tone is exasperation → をよそに. b) をものともせず always praises courage, which clashes with ぶらぶらしている. a) いかんで would need an outcome that changes with the criticism.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: （ ）、普通の人は一日中資料を調べるなんてできない。
items.qr: (___), futsuu no hito wa ichinichijuu shiryou o shiraberu nante dekinai.
items.en: A scholar might, but ordinary people just can't spend a whole day poring over documents.

opts.t: 学者のいかんによらず

opts.en: a scholar would be one thing, but

items.why: 学者 (extreme case: people who research for a living) vs 普通の人 (the ordinary case) + なんてできない (dismissive) → ならいざしらず. a) and b) treat 学者 as a variable with a range of values, which it isn't.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 5課 · 関連・無関係

items.q: うちの犬は、自分もこの家の家族の一人だと（ ）の顔をしてテレビを見ている。
items.qr: Uchi no inu wa, jibun mo kono ie no kazoku no hitori da to (___) no kao o shite terebi o mite iru.
items.en: Our dog watches TV with a look that seems to say, "I'm one of the family too."
items.why: 〜んばかり attaches to the ない-stem: 言わ + んばかり. a) 言うばかり means "does nothing but say", a different pattern. c) uses the full ない form, which is not the connection.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: ニュースを聞いて、彼は（ ）驚いた。
items.qr: Nyuusu o kiite, kare wa (___) odoroita.
items.en: Hearing the news, he was so startled he nearly jumped out of his skin.

opts.t: 飛び上がらんばかりに
飛び上がると言わんばかりに
飛び上がれんばかりに

items.why: 飛び上がる → ない-stem 飛び上がら → 飛び上がらんばかり. c) uses the potential/imperative-like stem れ, which is wrong. b) adds a "saying" that makes no sense — he didn't announce he'd jump.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 今にも（ ）子を置いて、母親はどこへ行ってしまったのだろう。
items.qr: Ima ni mo (___) ko o oite, hahaoya wa doko e itte shimatta no darou.
items.en: Where on earth has the mother gone, leaving behind a child who looks ready to burst into tears at any moment?
items.why: The blank modifies the noun 子, so it needs 〜んばかりの. a) 〜に is adverbial (modifies a verb). c) ばかり is noun-like and never takes な.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 彼女はその人の死を知って、（ ）声を上げて泣いた。
items.qr: Kanojo wa sono hito no shi o shitte, (___) koe o agete naita.
items.en: When she learned of that person's death, she wailed so loudly her throat seemed about to tear.

opts.t: みんなに聞こえんばかりの
涙があふれんばかりの
のどが張り裂けんばかりの
opts.en: as if her throat would tear

items.why: 〜んばかり needs an exaggerated image showing an unusual degree that fits the noun 声. A voice so loud it could tear the throat (c) is that. a) being heard by everyone is an ordinary, literal result — nothing extreme. b) overflowing tears describe eyes, not a voice.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 息子は「入るな」とばかりに、（ ）。
items.qr: Musuko wa "hairu na" to bakari ni, (___).
items.en: My son locked his room as if to say, "Keep out!"

opts.t: 部屋を出ていってしまった
部屋にかぎをかけてしまった
opts.r: heya ni kagi o kakete shimatta

items.why: とばかり means the words are not actually spoken (実際に声は出さない) but shown by an action matching them. Locking the door says "keep out". a) actually saying it contradicts the pattern. b) leaving the room doesn't express "don't come in".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 彼女は平凡なのはつまらないとばかりに、（ ）。
items.qr: Kanojo wa heibon na no wa tsumaranai to bakari ni, (___).
items.en: She wears unusual clothes, as if to say that being ordinary is boring.

opts.t: 変わった服を着ている

items.why: The behaviour must act out the unspoken words — dressing unusually is how you show "ordinary is boring". b) looking happy doesn't express that attitude. c) is a description/evaluation, not an action (態度・行動).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: その女の子は皿の上の野菜を見て、（ ）とばかり、横を向いた。
items.qr: Sono onna no ko wa sara no ue no yasai o mite, (___) to bakari, yoko o muita.
items.en: The little girl looked at the vegetables on her plate and turned her face away, as if to say, "I don't want to eat them."
items.why: Turning away (横を向いた) acts out refusal → 「食べたくない」. a) "looks tasty" and c) "wow, so much" would go with reaching for the food, not turning away.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: （ ）ともなく空を見ていたら、珍しい鳥が目に入った。
items.qr: (___) to mo naku sora o mite itara, mezurashii tori ga me ni haitta.
items.en: I was gazing idly at the sky when a rare bird caught my eye.
items.why: The connection is 動 辞書形 + ともなく, usually repeating the same verb (見るともなく見る). b) the volitional form contradicts "without intending to". c) 〜ている is not the permitted connection.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: （ ）ともなしにラジオをつけておくのが好きだ。
items.qr: (___) to mo nashi ni rajio o tsukete oku no ga suki da.
items.en: I like leaving the radio on without listening to anything in particular.

opts.en: listen to what (→ nothing in particular)

items.why: 何を V ともなしに = "without V-ing anything in particular" — no purpose (目的がなく). c) names a definite thing to listen to, which is a purpose. a) 何でも ("anything at all") is a different nuance and doesn't combine with ともなしに.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 父は日曜日、どこへ行くともなしに（ ）。
items.qr: Chichi wa nichiyoubi, doko e iku to mo nashi ni (___).
items.en: On Sunday my father went out alone, with no particular destination in mind.
items.why: The verb after ともなしに should be the same kind of action done aimlessly (前後に同じ動詞を使うことが多い) — going out matches 行く. a) staying home means he didn't go anywhere at all. c) thinking has nothing to do with going somewhere.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: （ ）わたしは彼を尊敬するようになった。
items.qr: (___) watashi wa kare o sonkei suru you ni natta.
items.en: I can't say exactly when it began, but I've come to respect him.
items.why: 〜ようになった describes a change over time, so the unclear element is when → いつから + ともなく. b) だれともなく means "someone unspecified", but the subject is clearly わたし. a) 何 is not a time/place/person question word, so it doesn't fit meaning B.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: さっきまであの木の枝に鳥が数羽いたが、（ ）飛んでいってしまった。
items.qr: Sakki made ano ki no eda ni tori ga suuwa ita ga, (___) tonde itte shimatta.
items.en: There were a few birds on that branch a moment ago, but they flew off to who knows where.
items.why: Flying off to somewhere needs a direction: question word + particle へ → どこへともなく (疑問詞と助詞の組み合わせ). b) lacks the particle that ties it to 飛んでいく. c) a count (何羽) isn't a time/place/person question word — and we already know there were 数羽.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 大川選手は走るのも速いしボールの扱いもうまい。（ ）サッカー選手だ。
items.qr: Ookawa senshu wa hashiru no mo hayai shi booru no atsukai mo umai. (___) sakkaa senshu da.
items.en: Okawa is a fast runner and great with the ball. He's a born footballer.
items.why: The connection is 動 ます-stem + ながら: 生まれ(ます) → 生まれながら, and before a noun it takes の. a) dictionary form and c) た形 are not allowed.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 祖母は（ ）戦争中の思い出話を語った。
items.qr: Sobo wa (___) sensouchuu no omoide banashi o katatta.
items.en: My grandmother, in tears, told us her memories of the war.
items.why: The blank modifies the verb 語った, so the adverbial 〜ながらに is needed — 涙ながらに is the fixed idiom meaning 泣きながら. a) 〜の would need a noun right after (涙ながらの訴え). b) 〜で is not a form of this pattern.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 久しぶりにふるさとを訪れた。（ ）古い家がわたしを迎えてくれた。
items.qr: Hisashiburi ni furusato o otozureta. (___) furui ie ga watashi o mukaete kureta.
items.en: I visited my hometown for the first time in ages. The old house, unchanged from the old days, welcomed me.
items.why: The blank modifies the noun 古い家, so 〜ながらの. c) 〜に would modify a verb (昔ながらに作られている). b) 〜で is not used.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 立ち食いそば屋は、座らないで（ ）そばを食べる店です。
items.qr: Tachigui sobaya wa, suwaranaide (___) soba o taberu mise desu.
items.en: A standing soba bar is a shop where you eat soba standing up rather than sitting down.
items.why: 〜ながらに(して) works only with a limited set of words (限られた言葉にしかつかない), and 立つ isn't one of them — so b) is out. For the state in which you do something, Japanese uses the て形: 立って食べる. c) 立ちながら (the "simultaneous action" ながら) is unnatural because 立つ is a change-of-posture verb.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 今度の議長はどうも甘い言い方をするきらいがあると、みんなに（ ）。
items.qr: Kondo no gichou wa doumo amai iikata o suru kirai ga aru to, minna ni (___).
items.en: The new chair is being criticised by everyone for having a tendency to put things too softly.
items.why: きらいがある is criticism (主に人を批判して言う), so what people do about it is 批判する. b) praise and c) being welcomed contradict the negative judgment.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: うちの子は（ ）きらいがある。
items.qr: Uchi no ko wa (___) kirai ga aru.
items.en: My child has a tendency to exaggerate things.
items.why: Only a bad tendency (良くない傾向) can come before きらいがある. Exaggerating is a fault; a) loving animals and b) tidying up are good habits.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: （ ）頭で考えるだけで行動に移さないきらいがある。
items.qr: (___) atama de kangaeru dake de koudou ni utsusanai kirai ga aru.
items.en: My younger brother has a tendency to just think things over in his head and never act on them.
items.why: きらいがある criticises another person and is normally not used about oneself (ふつう話者自身のことには使わない) → 弟. a) is first person. c) a place/country isn't the "person" whose habit is being criticised, and 日本では doesn't give the sentence a subject who "thinks only in his head".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: うちの夫は（ ）きらいがある。
items.qr: Uchi no otto wa (___) kirai ga aru.
items.en: My husband has a tendency to take up too many hobbies.

opts.en: spreads himself too thin with hobbies

items.why: きらいがある describes a tendency/habit (傾向・くせ) that the speaker sees as a bit bad. 〜すぎる shows a habitual excess. a) and b) are just facts/states about how many hobbies he has, not a tendency in his behaviour.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 彼女は、周りを（ ）の行動力の持ち主だ。
items.qr: Kanojo wa, mawari o (___) no koudouryoku no mochinushi da.
items.en: She has a drive so powerful it practically overwhelms everyone around her.
items.why: An unusual degree ("so strong it nearly overwhelms") → 〜んばかり, with the する-exception: 圧倒せんばかり. b) and c) とばかり describes an unspoken utterance shown through an action — 行動力 is a quality, not an act of "saying" anything.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 試験中ちょっと横を（ ）、カンニングと間違われた。
items.qr: Shikenchuu chotto yoko o (___), kanningu to machigawareta.
items.en: Just because I glanced sideways during the exam, I was mistaken for cheating.
items.why: The answer is the N2 form 〜たばかりに ("just because ~, something bad happened") — not one of this lesson's points; the set mixes it in as a trap. a) 〜んばかり would mean he "almost looked", but he actually did. b) とばかり needs an unspoken utterance acted out, which doesn't fit being suspected.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: だれに（ ）「春だなあ」とつぶやいた。
items.qr: Dare ni (___) "haru da naa" to tsubuyaita.
items.en: To no one in particular, I murmured, "Ah, it's spring."

opts.en: without saying it to anyone in particular

items.why: だれに言うともなく is the standard phrase "addressed to no one in particular" — meaning A of ともなく (no clear intention) with a question word. a) 言う is not one of the few words that take ながらにして. c) とばかり would mean he didn't say anything aloud, yet つぶやいた says he did.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 失敗して落ち込んでいたら、（ ）みんなに肩をたたかれた。
items.qr: Shippai shite ochikonde itara, (___) minna ni kata o tatakareta.
items.en: When I was feeling down after my failure, everyone patted me on the shoulder as if to say, "Cheer up!"

opts.t: 元気を出さんばかりに
元気を出したばかりに
元気を出せとばかりに
opts.r: genki o dase to bakari ni

items.why: The pat on the shoulder silently says "元気を出せ!" — a command-form utterance + とばかりに. a) 〜んばかり would describe the patters' own state ("almost cheering up"), which isn't the point. b) 〜たばかりに ("just because") gives a cause of something bad, which doesn't fit.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 運動がてら（ ）。
items.qr: Undou gatera (___).
items.en: I went out walking the dog, partly for some exercise.

opts.t: 運動場まで行ってきた

opts.en: went out to walk the dog

items.why: 〜がてら + a separate action that involves going out, which takes advantage of A. Walking the dog doubles as exercise. c) running 3 km is the exercise — nothing extra is being done. a) going to a sports ground is just the place to exercise, not a second errand.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）図書館に行った。
items.qr: (___) toshokan ni itta.
items.en: I went to the library while I was out shopping.
items.why: A should be an outing (移動を含む動作) different from the main purpose. Shopping is a separate trip; the library is the add-on. b) and c) borrowing / looking for books are the reason for going to a library — there's no "taking the chance" here.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）車の展示場をのぞいた。
items.qr: (___) kuruma no tenjijou o nozoita.
items.en: While out having fun, I took a peek at a car showroom.

opts.t: いい車を見つけがてら

items.why: 遊び here means "going out for fun", an outing during which you drop in somewhere. a) 見つける is a non-volitional result, not an outing (and finding a car is what you'd do at the showroom). b) hurrying is a manner, not an activity you can piggyback on — and it contradicts casually "peeking in".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）かたがた近いうちに恩師を訪ねようと思っている。
items.qr: (___) katagata chikai uchi ni onshi o tazuneyou to omotte iru.
items.en: I'm thinking of visiting my old teacher soon, partly to tell him I've found a job.
items.why: The noun is another purpose (別の目的) for the visit — a report is a classic one. a) 訪問 is the visit itself (訪ねる), so it's redundant. b) 食事 is not a polite purpose for calling on a teacher, and doesn't fit the formal tone of かたがた.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）かたがた、お宅に伺います。
items.qr: (___) katagata, otaku ni ukagaimasu.
items.en: I'll call at your home, partly to pay my respects.
items.why: ごあいさつ is a polite purpose for a visit → ごあいさつかたがた伺う. b) a holiday is a time, not a purpose. c) おじゃま (する) means visiting someone's home — the same act as 伺う, so it can't be the "other" purpose.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 叔母が体調を崩したと聞いたので、見舞いかたがた（ ）。
items.qr: Oba ga taichou o kuzushita to kiita node, mimai katagata (___).
items.en: I heard my aunt had fallen ill, so I went to help her out and to see how she was.
items.why: The book's rule: after かたがた, a verb of movement (行く・訪ねる) is typical. b) 〜に行った supplies that. a) 手伝った has no movement. c) sending fruit means you didn't go — and 見舞い is a visit purpose.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 彼は（ ）のかたわらNPOの活動をしている。
items.qr: Kare wa (___) no katawara enu-pii-oo no katsudou o shite iru.
items.en: Alongside his creative work, he is active in an NPO.
items.why: かたわら attaches to the main occupation (本業となる仕事). Creative work (writing, art) is his profession. a) living alone is a lifestyle, not work. c) a hobby is by definition not one's main job.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 母は（ ）かたわら翻訳の仕事もしている。
items.qr: Haha wa (___) katawara hon'yaku no shigoto mo shite iru.
items.en: Besides teaching maths, my mother also does translation work.
items.why: Teaching maths is a profession, so translation can run "beside" it. b) cooking dinner and c) listening to music are momentary daily activities — they'd take 〜ながら (simultaneous), not かたわら.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 山中さんは市役所に勤めるかたわら（ ）。
items.qr: Yamanaka-san wa shiyakusho ni tsutomeru katawara (___).
items.en: Alongside his job at city hall, Mr. Yamanaka is also active as a singer.

opts.t: 歌手としても活躍している
opts.r: kashu to shite mo katsuyaku shite iru
opts.en: is also active as a singer

opts.t: いつも忙しくしている
家では年を取った親の世話をしている
opts.r: ie de wa toshi o totta oya no sewa o shite iru
opts.en: looks after his elderly parents at home

items.why: After かたわら comes a social activity separate from the main job (本業とは別の社会的活動). A singing career fits. b) "being busy" is a state, not an activity. c) caring for one's parents is private family life, not a social activity.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 母は（ ）よく音楽を聞いている。
items.qr: Haha wa (___) yoku ongaku o kiite iru.
items.en: My mother often listens to music while she does the gardening.

opts.t: 庭仕事をするかたわら

items.why: Two actions at the same moment → plain 〜ながら. b) かたわら is for a main occupation plus a separate long-term activity; gardening isn't her job and listening to music isn't a social activity. a) かたがた needs a polite purpose for a visit and a movement verb.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 今回のことでは取引先に迷惑をかけてしまった。（ ）あいさつに行ってこよう。
items.qr: Konkai no koto de wa torihikisaki ni meiwaku o kakete shimatta. (___) aisatsu ni itte koyou.
items.en: We caused our client trouble over this matter. I'll go and pay them a visit, partly to apologise.
items.why: A formal business visit with a second polite purpose (apology) + a movement verb (行く) → かたがた. a) がてら is casual and needs an outing-type noun (散歩, 買い物); おわび isn't a movement activity you squeeze an errand into. b) an apology is not someone's main occupation.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）神社にお参りしてきた。
items.qr: (___) jinja ni omairi shite kita.
items.en: While out cherry-blossom viewing, I stopped by a shrine to pray.

opts.en: partly for (the polite purpose of) flower viewing

items.why: 花見 is a leisurely outing (移動を含む動作) and the shrine visit is squeezed into it → がてら. b) かたがた is for polite social purposes (お礼・報告・見舞い), not a leisure outing. c) flower viewing is not an occupation.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）ところをおじゃましました。
items.qr: (___) tokoro o ojama shimashita.
items.en: I'm sorry to have disturbed you on your day off.
items.why: The 🔗 line says 名 だ −の + ところを, so a noun links with の: お休みのところを. a) a bare noun can't attach directly to ところ; b) な is the link for な-adjectives, and お休み is a noun.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: すぐに（ ）ところを遅くなってしまいまして、申し訳ありません。
items.qr: Sugu ni (___) tokoro o osoku natte shimaimashite, moushiwake arimasen.
items.en: I should have informed you immediately, and I'm very sorry it has been so late.
items.why: This is the book's example ③ type, 〜べきところを: "when I ought to have done X (I didn't, and I'm sorry)". すぐに + 遅くなって only makes sense with "should have". a) お知らせするところを would mean "just when I was about to inform you" — no reason to apologise for lateness. c) お知らせした says it was already done, which contradicts 遅くなって.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: お忙しいところを（ ）。
items.qr: Oisogashii tokoro o (___).
items.en: Thank you for helping me when you were so busy.

opts.t: 手伝ってくださってありがとうございました
何かお手伝いしましょうか

items.why: The ⚠ note: 〜ところを is a courtesy phrase for having troubled the listener, followed by an apology or thanks. b) is thanks for the trouble. a) is encouragement and c) is an offer — in neither has the speaker troubled the listener.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: （ ）事故は起こらなかったものを、本当に残念なことになってしまった。
items.qr: (___) jiko wa okoranakatta mono o, hontou ni zannen na koto ni natte shimatta.
items.en: If they had been careful the accident wouldn't have happened — it's turned out truly regrettable.
items.why: ものを attaches to a sentence that supposes something contrary to fact (事実とは異なることを仮定した文). 〜ていれば … なかった is that counterfactual. b) 〜と is a general/habitual condition, not a regretful "if only". c) the て-form states a fact ("they were careful"), which contradicts the accident happening.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 会いたいと言っているんだから会ってあげればいいものを。どうして（ ）の。
items.qr: Aitai to itte iru n da kara atte agereba ii mono o. Doushite (___) no.
items.en: He's saying he wants to see you, so you could just meet him. Why won't you?
items.why: After 〜ものを comes the sentence describing the actual fact, which is the opposite of the "good" supposition. The supposition is "you should meet him", so the reality — and the source of the speaker's frustration — is that you don't. a) and b) agree with the supposition, so there would be nothing to complain about.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 行きたくないのなら、（ ）ものを。
items.qr: Ikitakunai no nara, (___) mono o.
items.en: If you didn't want to go, you shouldn't have gone (yet you did).

opts.t: 行かなければいけなかった
行かなければよかった

items.why: 〜ものを = "it would have been good if ~ (but it didn't happen)". Given 行きたくない, the good outcome is not going; the omitted reality is "you went". c) fits. b) "you should have gone" contradicts 行きたくないのなら. a) is an obligation, not a desirable counterfactual, so there's no regret for ものを to express.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: （ ）ものを、何も言わなければわかってもらえないよ。
items.qr: (___) mono o, nani mo iwanakereba wakatte moraenai yo.
items.en: If you talked to them they'd understand — but if you say nothing, they never will.

opts.en: even if you talk, they won't understand

opts.t: 話せばわからなくなる
opts.en: if you talk, they'll stop understanding

items.why: ものを needs the "things would have gone well" supposition (順当に成立していれば良かった). Only a) gives the good outcome that the reality (saying nothing) then spoils. b) and c) describe bad outcomes even if you talk, so there's no regret and no contrast with 何も言わなければわかってもらえない.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 試験の結果は予想していた通りだとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Shiken no kekka wa yosou shite ita toori da to wa ie, (___).
items.en: The exam result may have been just what I'd expected, but it was still a shock.

opts.t: あまりショックではなかった
opts.en: it wasn't much of a shock

opts.t: やはりショックだった

items.why: After とはいえ comes the speaker's evaluation against what the first half implies. "As expected" implies "no shock", so the contrary feeling — still a shock — fits (note やはり "even so"). a) follows naturally from 予想通り, so there's no contrast. b) is a bare fact, not an evaluation.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: あの党は支持率が落ちたとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Ano tou wa shijiritsu ga ochita to wa ie, (___).
items.en: That party's approval rating may have dropped, but it's probably not yet to the point of losing power.

opts.t: まだ政権を奪われるほどではないだろう
opts.r: mada seiken o ubawareru hodo de wa nai darou
opts.en: it's probably not yet bad enough to lose power

opts.t: 反省する態度が見られない
opts.en: it shows no sign of remorse

opts.t: また新しい政策を打ち出した

items.why: a) is a judgment (〜だろう) that pushes back against "approval fell" → "still not that bad". b) is a criticism, but it doesn't run against the first half (falling support and no remorse point the same way). c) is just a reported event, not the speaker's evaluation.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 有給休暇があるとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Yuukyuu kyuuka ga aru to wa ie, (___).
items.en: We may have paid leave, but actually taking time off is never easy.

opts.t: 昨年は休みを取らなかった
opts.en: I didn't take any leave last year

opts.t: 休みはなかなか取れないものだ
opts.r: yasumi wa nakanaka torenai mono da
opts.en: it's hard to actually take time off

opts.t: 1か月ぐらい休みを取りたい
opts.en: I want to take about a month off

items.why: b) is a general evaluation (〜ものだ) that contradicts "there's paid leave" → "but you can't really use it". a) is a single past fact — the book says the second half is not a mere fact. c) is a wish that actually follows from having leave, so there's no contrast.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: このテーブルは高いとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Kono teeburu wa takai to wa ie, (___).
items.en: This table may be expensive, but it's something you can use for a lifetime.

opts.en: it's something you can use all your life

opts.t: わたしは思い切って買った
opts.en: I took the plunge and bought it

items.why: a) is the speaker's evaluation that offsets "expensive" ("but worth it"). b) and c) are both narrated events, not evaluations; and c) "it broke quickly" doesn't answer "expensive" with a judgment that outweighs it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: （ ）といえども、勉強していなければいい点はとれないだろう。
items.qr: (___) to iedomo, benkyou shite inakereba ii ten wa torenai darou.
items.en: Even if it's an easy test, you probably won't get a good score without studying.
items.why: といえども overturns what you'd normally expect from X (そこから普通に予想されること). An easy test → you'd expect a good score → "but not without study". a) a first test and c) an entrance exam don't create the expectation "you'll score well anyway", so there's nothing to deny.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 失業したといえども、（ ）。
items.qr: Shitsugyou shita to iedomo, (___).
items.en: Even though you've lost your job, you mustn't fall behind on the rent.

opts.t: 家賃を滞納してはいけない
opts.r: yachin o tainou shite wa ikenai
opts.en: you mustn't fall behind on rent

opts.t: 彼はまた高い車を買った
opts.r: kare wa mata takai kuruma o katta

items.why: The second half of といえども is mainly an obligation / resolve / assertion, and it goes against the natural expectation ("jobless → you might be excused for not paying"). a) does both. b) is a narrated event (and about 彼, not a rule). c) is a command that simply follows from losing your job — no contrast.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 犯人でない証拠があるといえども、彼のことを（ ）。
items.qr: Hannin de nai shouko ga aru to iedomo, kare no koto o (___).
items.en: Even though there's evidence he isn't the culprit, we need to look into him.

opts.r: ki ni suru no desu ka

opts.t: 調べてみる必要がある

items.why: c) is an obligation/assertion (〜必要がある) — the typical ending for といえども — and it defies the expectation "proof of innocence → leave him alone". a) is a request and b) is a question; neither is the speaker's firm statement the stiff といえども calls for.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 彼女のお母さんだから、きっと静かな人だと思いきや、（ ）。
items.qr: Kanojo no okaasan da kara, kitto shizuka na hito da to omoiki ya, (___).
items.en: Since she's her mother, I assumed she'd be a quiet person — but she turned out to be very lively.

opts.t: とてもにぎやかな人だった
opts.en: she was a very lively person

opts.t: やはりとても静かな人だった
opts.r: yahari totemo shizuka na hito datta
opts.en: as expected, she was very quiet

opts.t: とてもきれいな人だった

items.why: と思いきや must be followed by a result different from the expectation. quiet → lively is the direct reversal. b) (やはり) confirms the expectation. c) is on a different axis (looks, not personality), so it doesn't contradict "quiet".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: お酒好きの松本さんは甘い物なんか好きじゃないと思いきや、（ ）。
items.qr: Osakezuki no Matsumoto-san wa amai mono nanka suki ja nai to omoiki ya, (___).
items.en: I assumed Mr. Matsumoto, who loves his drink, wouldn't care for sweets — but he ate as many as three pieces of cake.

opts.t: 辛いものばかり食べた
opts.en: he ate nothing but spicy food

opts.t: ケーキは食べないと言った
opts.en: he said he wouldn't eat cake

opts.t: ケーキを三つも食べた
opts.en: he ate three pieces of cake

items.why: Expectation: "doesn't like sweets". Only c) reverses it (and 三つも adds the surprise). a) and b) both confirm the expectation, so there is no 意外感 for と思いきや to express.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: あの弱小チーム、1回戦で負けると思いきや（ ）。
items.qr: Ano jakushou chiimu, ikkaisen de makeru to omoiki ya (___).
items.en: That weak little team — I thought they'd lose in the first round, but they made it all the way to the final.

opts.en: as expected, they lost in round one

opts.t: だれも勝つとは思わなかった
opts.r: dare mo katsu to wa omowanakatta

items.why: The second half must be the actual result that differed from the expectation — c). a) confirms the expectation (やはり). b) is just another expectation, not a result, and it agrees with the first half.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: いくつか間違いがある（ ）、トム君の日本語の文章は素晴らしい。
items.qr: Ikutsu ka machigai ga aru (___), Tomu-kun no Nihongo no bunshou wa subarashii.
items.en: Granted there are a few mistakes, but Tom's Japanese writing is excellent.
items.why: Fact (there are mistakes) + speaker's contrary evaluation (素晴らしい) = とはいえ. b) ものを needs a counter-to-fact supposition and a regret. c) と思いきや needs an expectation, and "there are mistakes" is a fact, not something the speaker had wrongly assumed.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 今日は一日中晴れる（ ）、午後からざあざあ降りになった。
items.qr: Kyou wa ichinichijuu hareru (___), gogo kara zaazaaburi ni natta.
items.en: I thought it would be sunny all day today, but from the afternoon it poured.
items.why: 一日中晴れる is an expectation that turned out wrong, and the second half is the surprising actual result → と思いきや. a) とはいえ and b) といっても both need the first half to be a fact; "it will be sunny all day" never became true.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 事情を知らなかった（ ）、失礼な質問をしてしまいました。
items.qr: Jijou o shiranakatta (___), shitsurei na shitsumon o shite shimaimashita.
items.en: Although I didn't know the circumstances, I asked a rude question (and I'm sorry).
items.why: Same shape as the book's 【3】④ (仕方がなかったとはいえ、ご迷惑をおかけしました): an admitted fact/excuse + "still, I was in the wrong". a) ところを needs the listener's ongoing situation (お忙しいところを); 知らなかった is the speaker's own ignorance. b) ものを would need a counterfactual (知っていれば…しなかったものを).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: もっとちゃんと薬を飲めば早く（ ）。
items.qr: Motto chanto kusuri o nomeba hayaku (___).
items.en: If you'd taken your medicine properly, you'd have got better sooner.
items.why: 〜ば…た + ものを at the end of the sentence, with the reality left unsaid — exactly the book's 【2】④ (手伝ったものを。). a) and c) must be followed by another clause, but the sentence ends at the blank; they also need the first part to be a fact, not a supposition.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: その計画は意義がある（ ）、多くの人の支持は得られないだろう。
items.qr: Sono keikaku wa igi ga aru (___), ooku no hito no shiji wa erarenai darou.
items.en: Even though the plan is worthwhile, it probably won't win the support of many people.
items.why: A fact (it has merit) whose natural expectation (people will back it) is denied by the speaker's assertion (〜だろう) → といえども. a) ものを needs a counterfactual supposition. c) と思いきや needs an already-happened surprising result; 〜得られないだろう is only a prediction.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: （ ）よく来てくださいました。
items.qr: (___) yoku kite kudasaimashita.
items.en: Thank you so much for coming all this way.
items.why: A set courtesy phrase of thanks for the trouble taken (遠いところを／お忙しいところを) — 〜ところを. b) といえども is stiff and leads to an obligation or assertion, not to thanks. c) ものを expresses regret about a counterfactual, which makes no sense in a welcome.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: わたしは、その仕事を引き受けるとは（ ）、結局やれなかった。
items.qr: Watashi wa, sono shigoto o hikiukeru to wa (___), kekkyoku yarenakatta.
items.en: I did say I'd take on the job, but in the end I couldn't do it.

opts.en: I'd have said it, if only…

items.why: 〜ものの is the N2 form from the 〔復習〕 box: "I did X, but what should have followed didn't" — a plain narrative contrast between two facts. a) とはいえ needs a speaker's evaluation after it, but 結局やれなかった is just a fact. c) ものを needs a counterfactual supposition (〜ば…たものを); here 言った really happened. Note the trap: ものの vs ものを differ by one kana.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 必要な学費とあれば、（ ）。
items.qr: Hitsuyou na gakuhi to areba, (___).
items.en: If it's tuition I actually need, my father will probably pay it for me.

opts.t: どうか払ってください
父は払ってくれるだろう

opts.r: dare ga harau n desu ka

items.why: After とあれば comes the speaker's wish, intention or judgment. b) is a judgment (〜だろう). a) is a request to the listener and c) is a question — neither is the speaker's own stance.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: （ ）とあれば、精いっぱい頑張ります。
items.qr: (___) to areba, seiippai ganbarimasu.
items.en: If it's a request from you, I'll do my very best.
items.why: とあれば needs a special condition (特別な条件) that motivates the result: "since it's you asking, I'll give it everything". a) everyday housework is the opposite of special. b) driving is just an activity, not a reason that would make someone try their hardest.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 家族のためとあれば、（ ）。
items.qr: Kazoku no tame to areba, (___).
items.en: If it's for his family, he'll probably do anything.

opts.t: どんなことをするんですか
opts.r: donna koto o suru n desu ka
opts.en: what kind of thing will you do?

opts.t: わたしに何ができますか
opts.r: watashi ni nani ga dekimasu ka

opts.t: 彼はどんなことでもするだろう
opts.r: kare wa donna koto de mo suru darou

items.why: Same rule — the second clause is the speaker's judgment (〜だろう). a) and b) are questions; とあれば doesn't lead into asking someone something.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: あんな人が委員長に（ ）最後、この会はだめになる。
items.qr: Anna hito ga iinchou ni (___) saigo, kono kai wa dame ni naru.
items.en: If someone like that becomes chair, this association is finished.
items.why: The fixed shape is た形 + ら最後 (or た形 + が最後): なったら最後. a) 〜と and b) 〜ば are other conditional forms that never combine with 最後.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 彼は怒ったら最後、（ ）。
items.qr: Kare wa okottara saigo, (___).
items.en: Once he gets angry, that's it — he'll never forgive you.

opts.t: 次の日にはもう忘れている
opts.r: tsugi no hi ni wa mou wasurete iru
opts.en: by the next day he's forgotten

opts.t: 絶対に許してくれない

items.why: 〜たら最後 is followed by something the speaker sees as very bad and lasting. c) "never forgives" fits. a) forgetting by the next day is actually a good outcome. b) a scary face is a natural, mild, momentary reaction — not the irreversible "end" that 最後 implies.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 麻薬は恐ろしいものだ。一度使ったが最後（ ）。
items.qr: Mayaku wa osoroshii mono da. Ichido tsukatta ga saigo (___).
items.en: Drugs are terrifying. Use them once and you can no longer stop by willpower alone.

opts.t: 意志があればやめられる
自分の意志ではやめられなくなる
opts.r: jibun no ishi de wa yamerarenaku naru
opts.en: you can't stop by your own will

opts.t: 医者に相談したほうがいい
opts.r: isha ni soudan shita hou ga ii

items.why: The second clause must describe the terrible, irreversible situation — b). a) is reassuring, which contradicts 恐ろしい and 最後. c) is advice, not a description of the bad state that results.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: わたしは卵アレルギーなので、卵が入っている食品をうっかり口にしたら最後、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi wa tamago arerugii na node, tamago ga haitte iru shokuhin o ukkari kuchi ni shitara saigo, (___).
items.en: I'm allergic to eggs, so if I accidentally eat anything containing egg, I break out in red spots all over my face.

opts.t: 顔中に赤いぶつぶつができる
opts.r: kaojuu ni akai butsubutsu ga dekiru
opts.en: red spots appear all over my face
I absolutely don't want to eat it

items.why: The result after 〜たら最後 is the bad event that inevitably follows — the allergic reaction, b). a) is the speaker's own countermeasure, not the disaster. c) is a wish, and it makes no sense after having already eaten it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: サラリーマンが毎日会社に（ ）ではだめだ。
items.qr: Sarariiman ga mainichi kaisha ni (___) de wa dame da.
items.en: An office worker who's late for work every day is hopeless.
items.why: The connection is plain form + ようでは: 遅刻するようでは. b) and c) use the volitional ending 〜(よ)う, which looks similar but is a different form entirely — it can't be followed by では.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 寄付の手続きがこんなに（ ）ようでは、寄付をする人が少なくなってしまう。
items.qr: Kifu no tetsuzuki ga konna ni (___) you de wa, kifu o suru hito ga sukunaku natte shimau.
items.en: If the donation procedure is this much of a hassle, fewer people will donate.
items.why: The 🔗 line: ナ形 だ −な (or −である) + ようでは. So 面倒なようでは (or 面倒であるようでは). a) the bare stem can't attach to よう; c) だ must be dropped.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 仕事がそんなに忙しいようでは、（ ）。
items.qr: Shigoto ga sonna ni isogashii you de wa, (___).
items.en: If your work is that busy, you'll ruin your health.

opts.t: 毎日充実しているでしょう

items.why: 〜ようでは predicts an undesirable result. a) is that warning. b) and c) treat being busy as something good — the opposite of what ようでは expresses.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 敬語がちゃんと使えないようでは、（ ）。
items.qr: Keigo ga chanto tsukaenai you de wa, (___).
items.en: If you can't use honorific language properly, you can't do customer-service work.

opts.t: しっかり勉強しなさい
接客の仕事はできない
日本人に聞いたほうがいい
opts.r: Nihonjin ni kiita hou ga ii
opts.en: you'd better ask a Japanese person

items.why: The ⚠ note: what follows is a prediction that something undesirable will happen. b) is exactly that. a) is a command and c) is advice — they tell the listener what to do instead of predicting the bad outcome.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 一日中アニメばかり見ているようでは、（ ）。
items.qr: Ichinichijuu anime bakari mite iru you de wa, (___).
items.en: If you watch nothing but anime all day, you won't have any time to study.

opts.t: アニメの専門家になれますよ
opts.r: anime no senmonka ni naremasu yo
opts.en: you could become an anime expert

opts.t: 勉強する時間がないでしょう
opts.r: benkyou suru jikan ga nai deshou
opts.en: you won't have time to study

opts.t: アニメの学校に行くといいですよ
opts.r: anime no gakkou ni iku to ii desu yo
opts.en: you should go to an anime school

items.why: b) is an undesirable prediction (〜でしょう). a) is a positive outcome, which clashes with ようでは's "bad state → bad result". c) is a suggestion, not a prediction.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 住民の理解と協力なしには（ ）。
items.qr: Juumin no rikai to kyouryoku nashi ni wa (___).
items.en: Without the residents' understanding and cooperation, this plan can't be carried out.

opts.t: この計画は実行できない
opts.en: this plan can't be carried out

items.why: なしには must be followed by a negative expression saying the thing can't be achieved. a) does that. b) is affirmative (and describes a side effect, not an impossibility). c) is volition.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 国の援助なしでは（ ）。
items.qr: Kuni no enjo nashi de wa (___).
items.en: Without government aid, this research can't continue.

opts.t: 民間の企業から寄付をしてもらおう
opts.r: minkan no kigyou kara kifu o shite moraou
opts.en: let's get donations from private companies

opts.t: わたしはこの研究班を辞める
opts.r: watashi wa kono kenkyuuhan o yameru

opts.t: この研究は続けられない

items.why: The aid is presented as indispensable, so the ending states what becomes impossible without it — c). a) is volition (〜よう) and b) is the speaker's decision; neither is the negative "can't happen" that なしでは requires.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: しっかり準備することなくしては（ ）。
items.qr: Shikkari junbi suru koto nakushite wa (___).
items.en: Without thorough preparation, you can't give a good presentation.

opts.en: you can't give a good presentation

opts.t: いい発表ができるんですか
opts.r: ii happyou ga dekiru n desu ka
opts.en: can you give a good presentation?

opts.t: 発表するのはやめよう

items.why: Negative ending required — a). b) is a question and c) is volition; both break the "X is essential, so without it Y is impossible" structure.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 結婚して（ ）くらいなら、一人で暮らすほうがましだ。
items.qr: Kekkon shite (___) kurai nara, hitori de kurasu hou ga mashi da.
items.en: If getting married means losing my freedom, I'd rather live alone.
items.why: くらいなら attaches to the dictionary form of a verb describing the worst case. b) is both. c) is the past (た形), which the 🔗 line doesn't allow. a) "wanting freedom" isn't a bad situation to avoid, and 欲しい is an adjective.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: わたしは料理が苦手なんです。自分で作るくらいなら、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi wa ryouri ga nigate nan desu. Jibun de tsukuru kurai nara, (___).
items.en: I'm hopeless at cooking. Rather than cook for myself, I'd be fine with just bread every day.

opts.t: おいしくできるわけがありません
opts.en: there's no way it'll taste good

opts.t: 料理教室に行って料理を習います
opts.r: ryouri kyoushitsu ni itte ryouri o naraimasu

opts.t: 毎日パンだけでもいいです
opts.r: mainichi pan dake de mo ii desu
opts.en: just bread every day is fine

items.why: The second clause is the option the speaker considers better than the worst case (cooking for herself). c) is that lesser evil. a) is a consequence of cooking, not an alternative to it. b) means she would cook after all — it doesn't avoid the worst case.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: わたしはエアコンが嫌いだ。エアコンを入れるくらいなら、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi wa eakon ga kirai da. Eakon o ireru kurai nara, (___).
items.en: I hate air-conditioning. Rather than turn it on, I'll put up with the heat.

opts.en: I'll put up with the heat

items.why: a) is the alternative the speaker prefers. b) and c) are consequences of turning on the air-conditioner — they would follow 〜と／〜たら, not くらいなら.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: あんな人に頭を下げて頼むくらいなら、（ ）。
items.qr: Anna hito ni atama o sagete tanomu kurai nara, (___).
items.en: Rather than bow my head and beg someone like that, I'll do it myself.

opts.t: 彼はいい気分になるだろう
opts.r: kare wa ii kibun ni naru darou

opts.t: だれもやってくれないだろう
opts.en: nobody will do it for me

items.why: b) is the preferable alternative chosen instead of the worst case (begging). a) is a consequence of begging. c) is a prediction, not an alternative the speaker would prefer.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: おいしいものを（ ）、わたしはダイエットなんかしなくてもいい。
items.qr: Oishii mono o (___), watashi wa daietto nanka shinakute mo ii.
items.en: If it means giving up delicious food, I don't need to diet at all.

opts.en: if it's a matter of holding back
if (you're in the bad state of) holding back

items.why: Worst case (giving up tasty food) → lesser evil (not dieting) = くらいなら. a) とあれば needs a special condition that justifies the speaker's action. b) ようでは needs a predicted bad result; "I don't have to diet" isn't one.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: ここでやる気を（ ）、彼は再び立ち上がれなくなるだろう。
items.qr: Koko de yaruki o (___), kare wa futatabi tachiagarenaku naru darou.
items.en: If he loses his motivation now, that'll be it — he'll probably never get back on his feet.

opts.en: once he loses it, that's it
if it's a matter of losing it

items.why: A trigger followed by an irreversible disaster (never getting up again) = たら最後. b) とあれば wants a special condition justifying an action. c) くらいなら needs a preferable alternative in the second half, not a dire prediction.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: （ ）、どんなことでもするんですか。
items.qr: (___), donna koto de mo suru n desu ka.
items.en: So if it's to make money, you'll do anything at all?

opts.t: 金もうけするくらいなら

opts.en: once you've made money, that's it

items.why: "If it's (for the special purpose of) money, (you'd do) anything" = とあれば, with どんなことでも as in the book's 【1】①. This is a rhetorical, critical question to the listener — it repeats the listener's stance back to them, so it doesn't break the "no questions" tendency in the way [1] Q3's genuine questions do. a) くらいなら would make money-making the worst case. c) たら最後 would need a disaster after it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 患者の気持ちを（ ）いい医者にはなれないだろう。
items.qr: Kanja no kimochi o (___) ii isha ni wa narenai darou.
items.en: Without understanding patients' feelings, you can't become a good doctor.

opts.t: 理解しなかったら最後
opts.en: once you fail to understand, that's it

opts.t: 理解することなくして

items.why: Understanding is the indispensable condition, and a negative (なれない) follows → V-dictionary + こと + なくして. a) といえば changes the topic, and makes no sense here. b) たら最後 needs a single trigger event leading to disaster; "failing to understand" is a lasting attitude, and 最後 sounds odd with a negative trigger.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 生まれたばかりなのに、今から子育てが大変なんて（ ）この先やっていけませんよ。
items.qr: Umareta bakari na noni, ima kara kosodate ga taihen nante (___) kono saki yatte ikemasen yo.
items.en: The baby's only just been born — if you're already saying child-rearing is tough, you won't cope with what's ahead.
items.why: An undesirable present state (already complaining) → a predicted bad result (you won't cope) = ようでは, exactly like 【3】②. b) なくして would make "saying it's hard" something indispensable — nonsense. c) くらいなら needs a preferable alternative, but やっていけません is a negative prediction.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: この仕事はだれが（ ）と、大差ない。
items.qr: Kono shigoto wa dare ga (___) to, taisa nai.
items.en: It makes little difference who does this job.

opts.en: so as to do / like doing

items.why: Verbs take the volitional form (う・よう形) before と: しようと. a) するよう is the "manner/so that" よう, a different word. c) だろう + と is only for adjectives and nouns (困難だろうと); a verb uses its own volitional form instead.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 母は、どんなに（ ）が、払うべき金は払ってくれた。
items.qr: Haha wa, donna ni (___) ga, harau beki kane wa haratte kureta.
items.en: However expensive it was, my mother always paid what needed to be paid.
items.why: The 🔗 line: イ形 かろう + と(も)・が → 高かろうが. a) 高いだろう is the pattern for な-adjectives/nouns (〜だろう), not い-adjectives. c) 高かったろう is a past conjecture, not on the connection line.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 母がどんなに説得しようが、父は（ ）。
items.qr: Haha ga donna ni settoku shiyou ga, chichi wa (___).
items.en: No matter how hard my mother tried to persuade him, my father didn't change his mind.
items.why: The second clause must show the result is not affected by the condition (前の条件に影響されない). c) does. b) means he was affected. a) is unrelated to whether the persuasion had any effect.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: どんなに便利なものだろうと、（ ）。
items.qr: Donna ni benri na mono darou to, (___).
items.en: However convenient something may be, I don't want to buy things I don't need.

opts.t: 要らないものは買いたくない
opts.en: I don't want to buy what I don't need

opts.t: 要らないものも買ってしまう
opts.en: I end up buying even what I don't need

items.why: "However convenient → I'm unmoved" — a) is the speaker's resolve, unaffected by convenience. b) shows the speaker being swayed by convenience, the opposite. c) is a general statement that has no connection with "however convenient".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: この先何があろうと、（ ）。
items.qr: Kono saki nani ga arou to, (___).
items.en: Whatever happens from here on, don't worry.

opts.r: shinpai de wa nai no ka

items.why: "Whatever happens" → a stance that ignores all possibilities: "don't worry" (the speaker's firm assertion). a) worrying is being affected by what might happen. c) is a question, not a judgment or resolve.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: わたしがあしたの会に参加しようとするまいと、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi ga ashita no kai ni sanka shiyou to suru mai to, (___).
